text:
alex: kicking off a kernel-aware aggregation sweep across cards to tune max tokens-per-batch. starting with the L4/A10/T4/A100/H100 matrix.

maria: nice. what's the hypothesis?

alex: hypothesis = current static max_tokens_per_batch is suboptimal when kernel selection flips (float16 vs int8 paths) and when KV cache hits vary. suspecting two failure modes: 1) small-seq tail latency spike on L4 with fused-prefetch kernel, 2) A100 underutilized when we cap by request-count instead of token budget.

tj: can you drop the perf numbers from the first sweep?

alex: pasted raw from profiler: 
```
A100 (canary): kernel=f16_matmul_v2, median RT=23ms, p99=68ms, tokens/batch=98k, kv_hit=0.73
H100 (canary): kernel=f16_matmul_v3, median RT=18ms, p99=54ms, tokens/batch=180k, kv_hit=0.79
L4 (canary): kernel=int8_fused_prefetch, median RT=28ms, p99=140ms, tokens/batch=42k, kv_hit=0.12
A10 (canary): kernel=int8_matmul, median RT=30ms, p99=90ms, tokens/batch=88k, kv_hit=0.45
T4 (canary): kernel=int8_matmul, median RT=45ms, p99=220ms, tokens/batch=36k, kv_hit=0.22
```

maria: that L4 p99 is wild. kv_hit only 12% explains the tail on small sequences?

alex: yeah, prefetch kernel adds ~3-4ms per request when no KV hit, but the batching behavior makes more requests coalesce -> longer scheduling jitter + memory pressure.

katie: did kernel selector change recently? we pushed fallback to fused-prefetch for seq<=64, right?

alex: deploy-bot rolled kernel-selector v1.9 to canary last night. deploy-bot: canary rollout complete for kernel-selector v1.9.

maria: v1.9 uses heuristics that prefer fused-prefetch when avg_req_len < 70 and kv_hit_rate > 0.5, else int8_matmul. seems wrong for L4 where kv_hit_rate is unstable.

tj: proposal: switch to token-budget-aware caps per-GPU instead of request-count thresholds. formula: max_tokens_per_batch = base_tokens * gpu_scale * (1 + kv_hit_rate * kv_scale). numbers we tried: base_tokens=40k, gpu_scale={T4:0.9,L4:1.1,A10:1.8,A100:3.0,H100:4.0}, kv_scale=0.6.

katie: did that reduce p99 on L4?

alex: quick A/B: with token-budget caps p99 for L4 dropped from 140ms -> 95ms; median unchanged. A100 throughput improved 9% because we allowed more tokens/batch when kv_hit high. T4 still p99 noisy.

maria: need guardrails for memory fragmentation. When we increase tokens-per-batch for A100/H100 we saw small increase in OOM-synced restarts on aged kernels.

alex: found regression trace: kernel f16_matmul_v2 alloc pattern triggers KV fragmentation under long-lived contexts. stack traces point to allocator churn during batching window.

devops: noted. opened infra ticket INF-4321 to track allocator tuning and prealloc thresholds.

katie: what's next operationally?

tj: action items:
- lower fused-prefetch preference for L4 when kv_hit < 0.25 (tj)
- enable token-budget caps for A100/H100 in canary and monitor OOMs (alex)
- add KV-hit smoothing (exponential window 30s) to kernel selector to avoid flip-flopping (maria)
- update rollout runbook with rollback thresholds: p99 increase >10% or OOMs >2/hr (katie)

alex: also adding a lightweight profiler hook to log per-batch selected kernel + kv_hit + tokens_batched so we can correlate in datadog. snippet: `select_kernel(metrics) -> record("kernel_choice", kernel, tokens, kv_hit)`

maria: sounds good. if we get stable kv smoothing we can probably increase A10 cap by ~10% which lowers cost per token.

devops: INF-4321 assigned to ops-allocator. will surface logs to #incidents if OOM spike.

alex: final note: avoid a single global cap. per-model and per-gpu-type caps with fallback policies (reject/queue) worked best in synthetic runs. sharing experiment CSV in thread: https://internal.redwood/sweeps/1799999999-aggregation-sweep.csv

katie: thanks. schedule follow-up sync after 24h of canary telemetry. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks all — will push smaller L4 kernel preference change in 15m and post results here.
